title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
abstract: arXiv:2610.27610v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) promises AI systems, such as self-evolving LLM agents, that become better at producing further improvements. Evaluating this promise requires separating product claims about the final system from process claims about the improvement process itself. Existing surveys specify the evidence these claims require, but how often studies report that evidence remains unmeasured. We examine this question through full-text coding of 114 eligible studies in a reproducible arXiv search frame frozen in October 2026, including 90 that describe their own systems as RSI. The codebook links claims to evaluation designs. Independent human coding, third-reader adjudication, and a separate blind coding of improver comparisons assess coding reliability. translated_title: 审计产品而非递归过程：递归自我改进声明背后的评估证据
translated_abstract: 递归自我改进（RSI）承诺了诸如自我进化的LLM智能体等AI系统能够在产生进一步改进方面不断提升。评估这一承诺需要将关于最终系统的“产品”声明与关于改进过程本身的“流程”声明区分开来。现有综述已明确了这些声明所需的证据，但研究实际报告这些证据的频率仍未被测量。我们通过对2026年10月冻结的可复现arXiv搜索框架中114项符合条件的研究进行全文编码来考察这一问题，其中包括90项将自身系统描述为RSI的研究。该编码手册将声明与评估设计相关联。通过独立的人工编码、第三方读者的裁定，以及对改进器比较的单独盲编码来评估编码的可靠性。在90项RSI研究中，90%在包含部分分离或未明确说明分离的宽泛标准下报告了超越开发任务的产品评估，而60%报告了评估……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文首次通过对114项递归自我改进（RSI）研究的系统性全文编码，量化审计了RSI声明背后产品评估与流程评估证据的实际报告频率，揭示了递归自我改进声明与其实际评估证据之间的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first quantitative audit of how often recursive self-improvement (RSI) claims are supported by actual product and process evaluation evidence, through systematic full-text coding of 114 studies, revealing gaps between RSI claims and their underlying evaluation evidence.
